catalysts: Tue Aug-12 08:30 — CPI m/m (fcst 0.1%) & Core CPI m/m (fcst 0.2%) / y/y (fcst 2.5%) — COOL=gold UP ~0.79%, HOT=gold DOWN ~0.70%; Wed Aug-13 08:30 — PPI m/m (fcst 0.2%) & Core PPI m/m (fcst 0.3%) — HOT=gold DOWN, COOL=gold UP; Fri Aug-14 08:30 — Retail Sales m/m (fcst 0.1%); Fri Aug-14 10:00 — UoM Consumer Sentiment (fcst 54.4) & Inflation Expectations (prev 4.2%) — elevated expectations=gold UP.
drivers: 1) US CPI/Core CPI (Tue) — primary rate-cut repricing lever; 2) US PPI/Core PPI (Wed) — pipeline inflation signal reinforcing or contradicting CPI; 3) Fed rate-cut timeline expectations and real yield moves; 4) USD direction driven by inflation data; 5) Geopolitical risk premium (background bid); 6) UoM Inflation Expectations (Fri) — sentiment anchor for longer-run inflation pricing.
filter: UP — Core CPI m/m below 0.2% forecast, CPI y/y below 3.4%, soft PPI, rising UoM inflation expectations, weak Retail Sales; DOWN — Core CPI m/m at or above 0.3%, CPI y/y at 3.5%+, hot PPI, strong Retail Sales signaling resilient demand.
phase: Gold enters the week in a data-heavy, Fed-sensitive phase. The Fed remains on hold, watching for confirmation that disinflation is resuming after the prior CPI y/y print of 3.5% and a flat core m/m. Real rates are modestly restrictive, capping gold's upside, but any softening in inflation data could revive rate-cut expectations and provide a bullish impulse. Geopolitical risk remains a background support. The dominant tilt is two-sided with a slight bearish lean into Tuesday's CPI: a hot print (Core CPI m/m ≥0.3%, CPI y/y holding at 3.5%+) would push the Fed further on hold and pressure gold; a cool print (Core CPI m/m ≤0.1%, CPI y/y below 3.4%) would be the week's clearest bullish catalyst. Key risk is a CPI upside surprise cementing a higher-for-longer narrative.
